answer:
Pending already is the keep-old-UI mechanism; a transition adds scoping, not a new renderer feature.
- Today: `Pending` keeps its previous content on a re-run until the new run resolves, latest run wins, unmount interrupts (README, pending.ts `Fork`/`Content`). A nested instance that re-runs on its own never shows the fallback.
- Re-runs are queued per instance with an epoch (dom.ts `queued`/`epoch`) and run to completion; there are no priority lanes, and none are needed for the model below.
- So `startTransition(write)` can only mean: apply the atom write, and mark the re-runs it triggers so a `Pending` they pass through keeps old content instead of showing its fallback. That is a flag carried by the triggered re-run, not a scheduler.
- What it cannot do without lanes: interrupt a long synchronous render or prioritise urgent input. State that limit in the ADR.
answer_gist: Pending already is the keep-old-UI mechanism; a transition adds scoping, not a new renderer feature.
question: Pending already keeps previous content on re-run; what extra guarantee does startTransition give with no lanes?
title: What keep-old-UI means here
